findings.remediation: Send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response. This is a one-line change in most web server configurations.
findings.impact: MIME sniffing can cause browsers to interpret content as a different type than intended, sometimes leading to script execution.

findings.remediation: Enable HSTS with a max-age of at least 6 months: `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15768000; includeSubDomains`.
findings.impact: Without HSTS, users are vulnerable to SSL-stripping attacks on first visit.

findings.raw_line: + [600050] Apache/2.4.25 appears to be outdated (current is at least 2.4.68).

findings.remediation: Disable directory listing in the web server configuration. For Apache, set `Options -Indexes` in the affected directory or globally. For nginx, remove `autoindex on`. For IIS, disable Directory Browsing.
findings.impact: Directory listings disclose file names and structure, aiding reconnaissance and exposing files not intended for public access.

findings.remediation: Block access to .git, .svn, and .hg directories at the web server level. Ensure deployment scripts do not copy VCS metadata into the web root.
findings.impact: Exposed Git metadata permits source code reconstruction, sometimes including hardcoded credentials and full application logic.

data.message: [007342] /: X-Frame-Options header is deprecated and was replaced with the Content-Security-Policy HTTP header with the frame-ancestors directive. See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Frame-Options

findings.raw_line: + [007342] /: X-Frame-Options header is deprecated and was replaced with the Content-Security-Policy HTTP header with the frame-ancestors directive. See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Frame-Options
findings.remediation: Set the X-Frame-Options header to DENY or SAMEORIGIN. Modern alternative: use the Content-Security-Policy `frame-ancestors` directive.
findings.impact: Missing frame protections allow the application to be embedded in attacker-controlled pages, enabling clickjacking.
